item.title: Growing up Online: How Digital Platforms Shape Adolescent Development
item.content:encoded:
Eoin Whelan, University of Galway

Hamed Qahri-Saremi, Colorado State University

Chelly Maes, Université Libre de Bruxelles

Christy M. K. Cheung, Hong Kong Baptist University

Uri Gal, University of Sydney

Monideepa Tarafdar, University of Massachusetts Amherst

This special issue examines how digital platforms shape adolescent developmental experiences across cognitive, emotional, psychological, social, and physical domains. With over 90% of adolescents regularly using social media and engaging with AI-powered applications, researchers are needed to understand both beneficial and harmful impacts of these technologies on youth aged 10-18.

The call welcomes empirical studies investigating how platform architectures, algorithmic systems, and AI technologies influence adolescent development through technical design choices. Research should examine specific mechanisms by which affordances, recommendation systems, and content curation shape adolescent experiences, as well as policy interventions and regulatory approaches aimed at protecting young users.

Studies must be based on primary or secondary data from adolescents, their caregivers, or digital trace data. The special issue invites diverse methodological approaches including behavioral research, design science, interpretive studies, and mixed methods, with particular interest in understanding generative AI's effects on youth development.

Appel publié par Journal of the Association for Information Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Platform architectures and affordances
  • Algorithmic curation and recommendation systems
  • Generative AI and chatbots for adolescents
  • AI literacy and digital resilience
  • Adolescent cognitive development and digital platforms
  • Emotional regulation and mental health impacts
  • Identity development online
  • Social relationships and peer interactions
  • Physical health and sleep patterns
  • Privacy and data protection
  • Digital divide and socioeconomic disparities
  • Policy and regulatory frameworks
  • Age verification systems
  • Content moderation approaches
  • Safety-by-design principles
  • Screen time controls and interventions
  • Misinformation and security risks
  • Adolescent information practices
  • Digital trace data analysis
  • Multi-platform engagement effects
